summary: Enhance your skills in criminal justice with our training course focused on inter-agency cooperation. Join us to improve collaboration and efficiency.
lede: Inter-agency cooperation in criminal justice training covers coordination among institutions from investigation through corrections and supervision. It is designed for criminal justice professionals, including police, prosecutors, court staff, forensic personnel and corrections or probation teams, who need to coordinate cases across agencies. Participants practise mapping mandates, improving handovers and information sharing, managing evidence transfers, preparing cases for trial and resolving disputes while protecting confidentiality, chain of custody, ethics and human rights.
audienceIntro: This course is crafted for criminal justice professionals who are integral to the justice process across multiple agencies and institutions.
audience: Police commanders, investigators, and case officers
Judicial officers, court administrators, registrars, and clerks
Forensic officers and crime scene personnel (labs
Probation, parole, and community supervision officers
Anti-corruption, organized crime, counter-terror, and special investigations
Victim support, child protection, and social services
Oversight bodies, inspectorates, internal affairs, and integrity
modules: Foundations of Inter-Agency Cooperation in Criminal Justice
Coordinating Case Preparation and Trial Readiness
Inter-Agency Cooperation in Corrections and Supervision
Dispute Resolution and Conflict Management Between Agencies
Integrity, Oversight, and Accountability in Cooperation
Crisis Coordination for High-Risk and High-Profile Cases
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 3 years of experience in criminal justice roles and familiarity with inter-agency operations.
